reviewer_scope: context-free oral-level review with independent web search
calibration: novelty plus one, capped at ten; other dimensions unchanged

reviews.title: Pareto-region proxy rank failure
nearest_prior_work: RegMix (arXiv:2407.01492) reports global proxy-target Spearman on the same Pile swarm; H001 instead tests top-quartile overlap and selected target regret on fixed halves of the 64-mixture grid.
DataDecide (arXiv:2504.11393) measures pairwise decision accuracy across 25 recipes, 14 sizes, and three seeds; H001 targets the extreme top region and RegMix argmin regret.
Can Small Training Runs Reliably Guide Data Curation? (arXiv:2512.24503) already centers top-k decision regret; H001 mainly changes the public grid, overlap statistic, and ID split.
ADMIRE-BayesOpt (arXiv:2508.11551) models scale-transfer uncertainty prospectively; H001 is a retrospective failure audit.
strongest_objections: The statement requires high global correlation but the support criterion has no global-Spearman threshold, a fatal statement-to-test mismatch.
Domain bootstrap variation is not target-training seed noise and can make the two-sigma regret misleading.
The two ID halves are not shown exchangeable; top-quartile overlap changes in 0.125 increments and objectives differ under raw versus standardized means.

reviews.title: Data-mixing-law optimum non-identifiability
nearest_prior_work: Scaling Laws for Optimal Data Mixtures (arXiv:2507.09404) fits the attacked laws and reports point optima; H002 estimates sampling uncertainty of the frozen law's argmin.
Data Mixing Laws (arXiv:2403.16952) fits response surfaces and selected mixtures but not bootstrap set-identification of the optimum.
Data Mixture Optimization (arXiv:2503.21023) uses posterior uncertainty prospectively for acquisition; H002 diagnoses deterministic-law instability retrospectively.
Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws (arXiv:2606.08167) reports lower-parameter extrapolated optima without confidence regions for the argmin.
strongest_objections: The loss-equivalence margin lacks a common held-out evaluation distribution; evaluating each optimum under its own fit is partly tautological.
Optimizer instability is not statistical non-identifiability without multistart convergence, KKT residuals, and separation of numerical failures.
The scale split, fixed target N and D, mixture-block availability, and bootstrap validity are underspecified.

reviews.title: OP-MIX pretraining coordinate inconsistency
nearest_prior_work: OP-Mix (arXiv:2605.15220) is the audited source; H003 tests the contract from 90/10 probe coefficients to final data ratios rather than empirical quality.
MergeMix (arXiv:2601.17858) also proxies data weights with merge weights; H003 uniquely derives and traces the affine coordinate map.
OLMix (arXiv:2602.12237) uses proxy-mixture coordinates intended directly as data ratios and does not create the same adapter-basis ambiguity.
RegMix regresses actual training ratios rather than weights over probes containing shared mixture mass.
strongest_objections: The universal statement is inconsistent with max and median error because error can be zero at the embedded old mixture.
The proposed old/new expression may not match five pretraining probes, whose natural map is q=0.9a+0.1u.
A coefficient difference is a defect only if the fitted optimum reaches the final sampler without expansion or inversion; source tracing is decisive.

reviews.title: ADMIRE multi-fidelity evaluation contamination
nearest_prior_work: ADMIRE-BayesOpt (arXiv:2508.11551) optimizes over a finite training pool; H004 interprets designated target rows as held-out evaluation and traces their lineage.
Data Mixture Optimization (arXiv:2503.21023) uses a separate 422/50 simulator split; H004 audits ADMIRE finite-pool lineage instead.
RegMix (arXiv:2407.01492) separates regression-training and target-mixture sets; H004 asks whether ADMIRE preserves an analogous separation.
Standard multi-fidelity BO permits paid acquisition of target-fidelity candidates; H004 alleges those candidates are also used as ostensibly out-of-sample evaluation labels.
strongest_objections: The page may conflate legitimate finite-pool acquisition with supervised test leakage and must identify an actual held-out-MSE estimand.
ID overlap alone is insufficient; a temporal trace must show a label entered fitting or metric construction before evaluation.
Changing either MSE or regret cannot establish both headline claims, and the IFT path repeats the same code rather than independently confirming it.

reviews.title: Point-prediction quality fails to certify mixture decisions
nearest_prior_work: Data Mixture Optimization (arXiv:2503.21023) reports scale-varying optima and R-squared before GP decisions; H005 conditions on high held-out R-squared and measures argmin regret.
RegMix (arXiv:2407.01492) uses global Spearman and a selected target mixture; H005 studies grouped scale holdout.
DataDecide (arXiv:2504.11393) already replaces predictive fit with pairwise decision accuracy.
Can Small Training Runs Reliably Guide Data Curation? (arXiv:2512.24503) already defines top-k decision regret.
strongest_objections: Leave-one-scale-out changes the published protocol, which trained with half of target-scale runs, so it does not audit the claimed frozen mapping.
Selecting at least one scale after inspection creates multiplicity; discovery must choose the confirmation scale.
Domain hash halves reuse models, mixtures, and scale noise; mixture bootstrap does not replace target-model seeds and must nest selection.

reviews.title: GRAPE convergence theorem admits a stationary counterexample
nearest_prior_work: GRAPE (arXiv:2505.20380) is the audited theorem; H006 gives a literal zero-source-gradient counterexample.
DoGE (arXiv:2310.15393) uses source-target gradient alignment but does not claim arbitrary smooth target objectives reach global epsilon optimality.
Group DRO (Sagawa et al., ICLR 2020) optimizes group losses that form the robust objective and does not bridge an unrelated target through vanishing source gradients.
Standard smooth nonconvex results guarantee stationarity rather than global optimality absent convexity or a progress condition.
strongest_objections: The sentence preceding the theorem invokes strong convexity, so the displayed omission may be typographical and the audit must target the literal statement only.
The proposed target is not strongly convex; conclusions cannot be extended to the intended strongly convex version or empirical algorithm.
Constant source losses work only if no incorporated source-target alignment or positive-progress assumption exists; every referenced assumption must be enumerated.
